rulings.challenge_claim: The Song.2.4 opening is argued from the absence of a formula anchor past Song.2.3 rather than from a positive tier-1 marker, so the row theme-splits a maximal she-voice run that properly spans Song.2.3-Song.2.7; the row's signal entry names a dodi anchor that stands in no verse of its own span; and the Song.2.6 WEB citation is straight-quoted and lower-cases the source's verse-initial word.
rulings.grounds: Diagnosis upheld, corrected span refuted. Upheld on bytes: nothing at the 2:3|2:4 junction is a tier-1 in-verse marker -- the last clause of oshb:Song.2.3 and the opening verb of oshb:Song.2.4 hold the same first-person speaker and the same third-masculine-singular referent, with no vocative, no suffix flip and no address-vocabulary anchor AT the cut, so the row's stated driver is anchor-absence plus a topic change (tier-2 continuity reasoning at best, not the tier-1 ground the hybrid granularity rule demands at a cut). Upheld on bytes: the row quotes the Song.2.6 clause with straight delimiters and lower-cases the verse-initial word -- that witness reads “His right hand embraces me.” (web:Song.2.6), and the row's string fails an exact-case substring check while passing case-insensitively; zero curly-quoted WEB runs stand anywhere in this cluster's rows. REFUTED, with the refuting bytes: the corrected span the challenge proposes (Song.2.3-Song.2.7) cannot stand. Song.2.3 is the answering member of an attested tier-1 alternation pair -- רַעְיָתִ֖י (oshb:Song.2.2, tier: byte), his address word for her, answered by דּוֹדִ֖י (oshb:Song.2.3, tier: byte), her word for him -- inside the hinnakh/hinnekha exchange that the owner ruling holds whole as one dialogue unit; moving Song.2.3 into a she-voice run would both break that whole-held zone and split an attested anchor pair. The seam is therefore real and inherited from the preceding zone's close; only the row's STATEMENT of it is defective. Signal-entry sub-claim REFINED, not upheld: no dod-family token stands in Song.2.4-Song.2.6 (verified verse by verse), so the challenge's byte observation is right, but the signal field contract records the signal CLASS consulted, and consulting the address-vocabulary class to establish that no anchor survives is within the contract -- the defect is the rationale's reliance on that absence, not the field entry. NEW FINDING (neither primary): the ahavah citation blends units -- the row calls the Song.2.4 form a token and then says 'one of ten', while the true objects are 10 VERSES and 11 TOKENS (MT 8:7 carries two); the parenthetical names verses, the prose object does not.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the anchor-absence driver with the positive warrant that the preceding unit is a whole-held dialogue exchange closing at Song.2.3, citing the attested anchor pair (his address word at oshb:Song.2.2, hers at oshb:Song.2.3, tier: byte) as the reason this row opens at Song.2.4; delete the 'no formula anchor survives past Song.2.3' phrasing as a driver. Re-cut the Song.2.6 citation as a curly-quoted, exact-case run paired with its inline web: ref. device_notes: name the swept object and unit for the ahavah claim (10 verses, 11 tokens). Tests the cure must pass: the span must still open at Song.2.4 (a re-cut to Song.2.3 fails the whole-held dialogue-zone rule and splits the oshb:Song.2.2/oshb:Song.2.3 anchor pair -- this is the test that kills the challenge's own proposed replacement); the WEB run must pass an exact-case contiguous substring check against that witness; the ahavah citation must name object and unit before its digit. Span change: none proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: No tier-1 marker stands at the row's opening cut; an undisclosed apple-token link straddles that same seam; the row's no-addressee ground is contradicted by the imperatives in its own middle verse and is inconsistent with the criterion applied at Song.2.15; and the closing seam is argued only from an English rendering while the embrace colon's recurrence before the later adjuration goes undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Three sub-findings upheld exactly on re-derivation, one re-labelled. (1) Same defect as the LF item at the cut: verified, no tier-1 in-verse marker at 2:3|2:4. (2) Cross-seam token link verified with the object named: the stem shared by the two apple forms sweeps to 4 verses at skeleton tier (MT 2:3, MT 2:5, MT 7:9 = WEB 7:8, MT 8:5 -- the offset-zone dual is arithmetically right), two of them on opposite sides of this row's own opening seam, and both witnesses carry the link; the row discloses nothing. The tier is skeleton, not byte: the two attested forms differ in number and pointing, so the honest statement is a shared-stem link, not a formula recurrence. (3) The no-addressee ground is byte-false INSIDE the row's own span: סַמְּכ֨וּנִי֙ בָּֽאֲשִׁישׁ֔וֹת רַפְּד֖וּנִי (oshb:Song.2.5, tier: byte) is two plural imperatives carrying first-person-singular object suffixes -- an explicit addressee -- and that other witness renders them as imperatives too; the inconsistency charge also holds, since the plural-imperative-addressee feature is what drives the cut at Song.2.15 in this same cluster. (4) RE-LABELLED inside the uphold: the byte fact is verified -- וִימִינ֖וֹ תְּחַבְּקֵֽנִי (oshb:Song.2.6, tier: byte) recurs at MT 8:3 at SKELETON tier only (skeleton sweep of that colon: 2 verses, MT 2:6 and MT 8:3; the byte and accent tiers each return 1 verse because the later site carries an extra meteg, and the verse's left-hand colon differs by a prefixed preposition and sweeps to 1 verse, which is how the pair escapes an exact sweep) -- and it stands immediately before the MT 8:4 adjuration, so an embrace-line-then-adjuration sequence recurs; but that parallel SUPPORTS this row's own 2:6|2:7 close rather than arguing a rival to it, so it is an undisclosed strengthener, not a rival cut. The closing-seam complaint stands on its own: the seam is argued from an English rendering with no Hebrew quoted at the closing verse.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: delete the no-addressee ground outright and re-state the span's texture from its own bytes (a first-person voice that includes an addressed plural imperative at Song.2.5); ground the closing seam in Hebrew by quoting the embrace colon from oshb:Song.2.6 (tier: byte) rather than in translation. device_notes: disclose the apple-stem link across the opening seam with its tier and digit (skeleton sweep: 4 verses, MT 2:3, MT 2:5, MT 7:9 = WEB 7:8, MT 8:5), and disclose the embrace-colon recurrence at MT 8:3 (skeleton sweep: 2 verses) as a parallel supporting this close. Reconcile the plural-imperative criterion with its use as a cut driver at Song.2.15 in one clause. Tests the cure must pass: no stated ground may survive that the row's own span bytes contradict (the Song.2.5 imperatives are the test that killed the original); every cross-seam device named must carry tier AND digit AND its offset-zone dual where one applies; the same feature must not be a driver in one row and absent from the criterion in another. Span change: none proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the Song.2.9 WEB citation ellipsis-splices two non-adjacent clauses, silently drops an intervening sentence, lower-cases a verse-initial word and is straight-quoted, while the row's boundaries are sound. OL: the qol-dodi recurrence carries no tier and is not byte tier at its second site, and a byte-attested colon brackets MT 2:8-2:17 across the row's own closing seam undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: DISTINCT defects, both upheld; the two primaries did not overlap on this row, and both agree the boundaries themselves are sound (re-derived: the formula opens the movement immediately after the adjuration bracket, and עָנָ֥ה דוֹדִ֖י וְאָ֣מַר לִ֑י (oshb:Song.2.10, tier: byte) is a genuine tier-1 frame verb introducing quoted speech). LF upheld: the row presents 'he stands behind our wall... he glances through the lattice' as one run against a single web: ref; that witness reads “Behold, he stands behind our wall! He looks in at the windows. He glances through the lattice.” (web:Song.2.9), so a whole sentence is dropped inside the ellipsis and the second fragment lower-cases a verse-initial word -- the presented run fails an exact-case check and fails a contiguous check even case-insensitively; delimiters are straight, not curly. OL upheld: the row's recurrence claim carries no tier at all, and the tier is not byte -- ק֣וֹל דּוֹדִ֔י (oshb:Song.2.8, tier: byte) reaches only accent_stripped at the second site, whose attested shape is ק֣וֹל דּוֹדִ֣י דוֹפֵ֗ק (oshb:Song.5.2, tier: byte); the honest object is a 2-verse recurrence at accent_stripped/skeleton tier (MT 2:8, MT 5:2), so the DIGIT the row cites is right and only the tier is missing. OL's bracket upheld with its object verified: the gazelle-and-fawn colon לִצְבִ֔י א֖וֹ לְעֹ֣פֶר הָֽאַיָּלִ֑ים (oshb:Song.2.9, tier: byte) and לִצְבִ֗י א֛וֹ לְעֹ֥פֶר הָאַיָּלִ֖ים (oshb:Song.2.17, tier: byte) share a 19-character consonantal run whose skeleton sweep returns 3 verses (MT 2:9, MT 2:17, MT 8:14); the two chapter-2 members sit on opposite sides of this row's closing seam and bracket MT 2:8-2:17, and no row in the stretch discloses it. The spelling-split caution is verified too: the likeness verb is written with vav at MT 2:9 (skeleton sweep: 1 verse) and without it at MT 2:17 and MT 8:14 (skeleton sweep: 2 verses), so an exact sweep of either spelling hides a member.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: re-cut the Song.2.9 citation as a contiguous curly-quoted exact-case run, or as two separately-quoted runs each paired with its own inline web: ref -- no ellipsis across a dropped sentence. Tier-label the qol-dodi recurrence at the tier a collation proves (byte at oshb:Song.2.8; accent_stripped at the second site, attested there in a longer shape), keeping the 2-verse digit. device_notes: disclose the gazelle-and-fawn colon across the closing seam with tier and digit (skeleton sweep: 3 verses, MT 2:9, MT 2:17, MT 8:14) and name the likeness-verb spelling split before any digit is reused. Tests the cure must pass: the WEB run must pass a contiguous exact-case substring check against that witness (the dropped sentence is the test that killed the original); the recurrence claim must carry the tier a collation returns at EVERY cited site, not at the first only; the cross-seam device must be disclosed with tier and digit. Span change: none proposed -- both primaries affirm the boundaries.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the Song.2.14 WEB citation is verbatim in content but straight-quoted rather than curly, a register-only defect. OL: the frame-verb wording attributed to web:Song.2.10 is not that witness's rendering, and the blossom-token chain straddling the closing seam is undisclosed; the second-feminine-singular marker case and the disclosure symmetry are otherwise the cluster's strongest.
rulings.grounds: DISTINCT defects. The refinement is of severity and of which finding is load-bearing: the LF item rates this row's only defect 'low' and register-only, which understates the row, because the substantive defect it missed is a misattributed witness rendering. Verified: the row gives the frame verb as an answered-and-said wording attributed to web:Song.2.10, but that witness reads “My beloved spoke, and said to me,” (web:Song.2.10) -- the row's string fails a substring check against that witness even case-insensitively, so the wording ascribed to the cited witness is not its wording. The Hebrew עָנָ֥ה דוֹדִ֖י וְאָ֣מַר לִ֑י (oshb:Song.2.10, tier: byte) does support an answered-gloss, but this row quotes no Hebrew at that clause, so its own frame-verb ground is translation-dependent on a rendering that witness does not carry. LF's register point is separately verified and real: the Song.2.14 run is an exact-case verbatim substring of that witness but is delimited with straight marks, and this cluster carries zero curly-quoted WEB runs while the corpus uses the curly convention elsewhere -- so the departure is local, not a book-wide convention. OL's cross-seam finding verified with object and tier: the blossom token is byte at each of its own sites, סְמָדַ֖ר (oshb:Song.2.13, tier: byte) and סְמָדַֽר (oshb:Song.2.15, tier: byte), and the link between them is skeleton tier, sweeping to 3 verses book-wide (MT 2:13, MT 2:15, MT 7:13 = WEB 7:12 -- dual arithmetically right), two of the three sitting on opposite sides of this row's closing cut. Verified as correct and NOT defective: the disclosure symmetry OL credits is real -- both ketiv/qere-bearing verses in span and both marked verses in span are named, and no quoted slice crosses the ketiv word inside the Song.2.13 line.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: either replace the frame-verb wording with that witness's actual rendering, curly-quoted with its inline web: ref, or re-anchor the ground on the Hebrew frame verb spliced from oshb:Song.2.10 (tier: byte) with the gloss marked as a gloss; re-cut the Song.2.14 citation into curly quotes with its inline web: ref. device_notes: disclose the blossom-token link across the closing seam with tier and digit (skeleton sweep: 3 verses, MT 2:13, MT 2:15, MT 7:13 = WEB 7:12). Tests the cure must pass: every English run attributed to a web: ref must pass an exact-case verbatim check against THAT witness (this is the test that killed the original, and the all-straight-quote habit is exactly what let it through unchecked); the cross-seam device must carry tier, digit and its offset-zone dual. Span change: none proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the literary-form judgment and the low-confidence hold are sound, but the Song.2.15 WEB citation lower-cases the source's verse-initial word and uses straight quotes. OL: isolating this verse is contested by a byte-attested blossom-and-vineyard chain straddling the row's own opening seam that is nowhere disclosed.
rulings.grounds: DISTINCT defects, both upheld. LF verified: the row quotes the foxes couplet with a lower-cased verse-initial word; that witness reads “Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that plunder the vineyards; for our vineyards are in blossom.” (web:Song.2.15), and the row's run fails an exact-case substring check while passing case-insensitively, with straight delimiters. OL verified: סְמָדַֽר (oshb:Song.2.15, tier: byte) shares its blossom token with סְמָדַ֖ר (oshb:Song.2.13, tier: byte); the skeleton sweep of that token returns 3 verses book-wide (MT 2:13, MT 2:15, MT 7:13 = WEB 7:12), so two of the three sites sit two verses apart across this row's own opening seam and both witnesses carry the link. Under the cross-seam standard a device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed, and a single-verse isolation already held at low confidence is where that disclosure is most load-bearing -- OL's medium severity is the right one, not LF's low. OL's vineyard caution is verified and correctly stated as a caution rather than a defect: the bare spelling sweeps to 1 verse (MT 8:11) while the suffixed spellings standing in this verse escape that sweep, so no vineyard digit may be used in either direction without naming the attested spelling. Verified as correct and NOT defective: the row's positive grounds -- the imperative clause re-collates byte at its own ref, the verse carries an addressee and a speaking group but no speaker-gender marker, no address anchor stands in it -- and the bespoke low-confidence hold, which both primaries affirm and the owner ruling anticipates for this verse.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: disclose the blossom-token chain across the opening seam with tier and digit (skeleton sweep: 3 verses, MT 2:13, MT 2:15, MT 7:13 = WEB 7:12) and state in one sentence why the isolation survives it -- the shared token is a skeleton-tier imagery link, not a voice or formula anchor -- or, if it does not survive, disclose the fold into the preceding unit as the rival. boundary_rationale: re-cut the Song.2.15 citation as a curly-quoted exact-case run with its inline web: ref. Tests the cure must pass: the WEB run must pass an exact-case substring check (the lower-cased verse-initial word is the test that killed the original); the cross-seam device must be disclosed with tier, digit and its offset-zone dual; any vineyard digit must name its attested spelling first. Span change: none proposed -- the isolation is upheld, the disclosure is what is missing.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the formula identifications and boundaries are tier-1 sound, but the Song.2.17 WEB citation uses straight rather than curly quotes. OL: the stated ground of no addressee or gender-marked interruption is contradicted by that verse's own bytes, the gazelle-and-fawn bracket reaching back to MT 2:9 is undisclosed, and the day-cooling recurrence carries no tier though byte tier is available.
rulings.grounds: DISTINCT defects; the OL item is the substantive one and is upheld in full, the LF item is a real but register-only finding on the same row. Verified: the row states that the second verse continues with 'no addressee or gender-marked interruption' and then, in the same sentence, cites the imperative addressed to him -- and the bytes side with the second clause. דּוֹדִ֥י לִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י ל֔וֹ (oshb:Song.2.16, tier: byte) is third-person reference throughout, with no addressee; סֹב֩ דְּמֵה לְךָ֨ דוֹדִ֜י (oshb:Song.2.17, tier: byte) turns to direct address with a second-masculine-singular suffix, final kaf plus qamats, contrasting byte-visibly with the second-feminine-singular final kaf plus sheva of מַרְאַ֔יִךְ (oshb:Song.2.14, tier: byte). A gender-marked addressee therefore IS introduced at the 2:16|2:17 junction, and the same feature drives a cut at Song.2.15 in this cluster, so the criterion is applied inconsistently. The SPAN can still stand -- one speaker across both verses, closed by the day-cooling formula -- but on single-speaker continuity, which the owner's moderate policy rates tier-2 corroboration, not the tier-1 ground the row states. Tier omission verified and cheaply curable: the day-cooling colon is character-identical at both sites -- עַ֤ד שֶׁיָּפ֨וּחַ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְנָ֖סוּ הַצְּלָלִ֑ים (oshb:Song.2.17, tier: byte) and עַ֤ד שֶׁיָּפ֨וּחַ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְנָ֖סוּ הַצְּלָלִ֑ים (oshb:Song.4.6, tier: byte) -- so byte tier was available and none was named. Bracket verified: the gazelle-and-fawn colon at oshb:Song.2.17 shares a 19-character consonantal run with MT 2:9 and MT 8:14 (skeleton sweep: 3 verses), the chapter-2 members bracketing MT 2:8-2:17 across three of this cluster's seams undisclosed. LF verified separately: the Song.2.17 run is exact-case verbatim in that witness but straight-delimited. Verified as correct and NOT defective, as OL states: the mutual-belonging shape is quoted in its attested his-mine order rather than harmonized with the flipped or desire variants; the mark at that verse is disclosed as single-witness tier-3 corroboration; the grazing participle is not blended with the address word of the same consonantal neighbourhood.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: delete 'no addressee or gender-marked interruption'; re-ground the unit on single-speaker continuity labelled tier-2 corroboration PLUS the mutual-belonging formula site, and disclose in one clause that Song.2.17 turns to second-masculine-singular address (splice the address run from oshb:Song.2.17, tier: byte, against the second-feminine-singular form at oshb:Song.2.14). device_notes: tier-label the day-cooling recurrence at byte tier, and disclose the gazelle-and-fawn bracket back to MT 2:9 with tier and digit (skeleton sweep: 3 verses, MT 2:9, MT 2:17, MT 8:14). boundary_rationale: re-cut the Song.2.17 citation into curly quotes with its inline web: ref. Tests the cure must pass: no stated ground may be contradicted by a clause of the row's own next sentence or by in-span bytes (the second-masculine-singular suffix is the test that killed the original); the recurrence claim must carry the tier a collation proves; the addressee criterion must read the same here as at Song.2.15. Span change: none proposed -- the span survives on re-grounded evidence.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the formula's fourfold recurrence is the tier-1 spine, but the row overclaims byte identity at the third site, whose accent differs. OL (high): the same tier overclaim is machine-refuted at that site, AND the narrated-past-tense characterization that carries the unit type is contradicted by the bytes at three points.
rulings.grounds: CONVERGENT on the first defect -- the SAME defect, found independently and byte-confirmed here; DISTINCT on OL's second. Tier overclaim UPHELD: the formula spliced from its first site, שֶׁאָהֲבָ֖ה נַפְשִׁ֑י (oshb:Song.3.1, tier: byte), re-collates byte at oshb:Song.3.2 and oshb:Song.3.4 but only accent_stripped at oshb:Song.3.3, whose attested pointing is שֶׁאָהֲבָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֖י (oshb:Song.3.3, tier: byte); the reverse test agrees. The row's 'tier: byte each' is therefore false at one of the three cited sites. Refinement of the object BOTH primaries state imprecisely: the run differs at TWO accent positions, not one -- LF names only the accent on the first word (tipeha at the three sites, merkha at the third), while the second word also differs (etnahta at Song.3.1, Song.3.2 and Song.3.4 against tipeha at Song.3.3); the honest object is OL's, a 5-verse skeleton-tier formula (MT 1:7 plus MT 3:1-3:4, verified), four sites in span, byte-identical at three of them. SEVERITY REFINED DOWN from high: OL's second finding is byte-real but does not carry what OL says it carries. Verified real: אָק֨וּמָה נָּ֜א וַאֲסוֹבְבָ֣ה and אֲבַקְשָׁ֕ה (oshb:Song.3.2, tier: byte) are prefix-conjugation forms with a final he, the first standing beside the entreaty particle; אַרְפֶּ֔נּוּ (oshb:Song.3.4, tier: byte) is likewise prefix-conjugation; רְאִיתֶֽם (oshb:Song.3.3, tier: byte) carries the second-person-plural ending and is a question put to the watchmen named in the same verse -- so the row's blanket 'narrated past-tense verbs' list is wrong at the rising, the going-about, the seeking, the not-letting-go and the watchmen question. NOT carried: the unit type does not fall with it. The episode's frame verbs ARE suffix-conjugation -- בִּקַּ֕שְׁתִּי (oshb:Song.3.1, tier: byte), מְצָא֨וּנִי֙ (oshb:Song.3.3, tier: byte), אֲחַזְתִּיו֙ (oshb:Song.3.4, tier: byte) -- and this seek-find night episode is the owner-named operative zone for the narrated-event-chain category, so the defect is a prose verb-form mischaracterization, not a unit_type failure: medium, not high. NEW FINDING (neither primary): adjacent-mark disclosure is asymmetric -- the row names the single-witness mark standing immediately before its opening but not the one standing at MT 3:5, the verse whose formula the row argues as its own close; the disclosure standard is unconditional and symmetric across both seams.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: correct the tier claim to what collation returns site by site (byte at oshb:Song.3.2 and oshb:Song.3.4, accent_stripped at oshb:Song.3.3) and state the honest object -- a 5-verse skeleton-tier formula, four sites in this span, the fifth outside it. Recast the verb-form gloss: name the suffix-conjugation frame verbs as the narrated spine and the rising/going-about/seeking/not-letting-go as prefix-conjugation volitive shapes, with the watchmen line marked as quoted second-person-plural address inside the episode; keep unit_type narrative_sequence and rest it on the suffix-conjugation frame. device_notes: complete the mark-disclosure symmetry by naming the single-witness mark at MT 3:5 at the argued close alongside the one before the opening, both as tier-3 corroboration. Tests the cure must pass: every 'verbatim/byte-identical' claim must be collate-proven at EVERY cited site, not at the first (this is the test that killed the original); the verb-form gloss must survive a per-token check against the pointed bytes; mark disclosure must be symmetric across both seams, as a sweep and not a spot fix. Span change: none proposed -- both primaries affirm the boundaries and the closing seam is byte-grounded.

supported_sample.claim_checked: That this verse opens the first of four attested adjuration sites in the book (sweep: 4 verses) in the FULL shape carrying both the gazelle clause and the doubled adjuration verb, and that MT 3:5 is byte-identical to it.
supported_sample.notes: Re-derived independently, object first then digit. The skeleton sweep of the adjuration verb in its first-person shape returns exactly 4 verses (MT 2:7, MT 3:5, MT 5:8, MT 8:4); the bare root sweep returns 5, the fifth being the daughters' quoted-back form at MT 5:9 -- a different speech role, correctly excluded from the site count, and no 'seven' or 'sated' reading exists in this book to blend in. The FULL shape is byte-verified as the discriminator: the gazelle clause בִּצְבָא֔וֹת א֖וֹ בְּאַיְל֣וֹת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה and the doubled verb אִם תָּעִ֧ירוּ וְֽאִם תְּעֽוֹרְר֛וּ (oshb:Song.2.7, tier: byte for both) each byte-sweep to exactly 2 verses (MT 2:7 and MT 3:5) and stand in neither MT 5:8 nor MT 8:4, so the three attested shapes are not harmonized. MT 2:7 and MT 3:5 are character-for-character identical across all 160 characters, so the row's byte-identity statement is exact. The single-witness mark at MT 2:7 is real in the inventory and is named as tier-3 corroboration with driver status explicitly denied. One available strengthener, not a defect: this verse carries one paseq seg (count-only, single-witness, position unsourceable), which the row does not cite in either direction.
